taxonomy.note: Older Texas references frequently use Merremia dissecta or Ipomoea sinuata.

project_inclusion.regional_note: Kew treats Texas within the native range. Austin and NPSOT sources also treat Alamo vine as a Texas/Central Texas plant under the older name Merremia dissecta.

morphology_keys.habit: Trailing or twining herbaceous vine; stems sparsely hirsute to glabrous.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Blades about 4–7 cm long by 4–10 cm wide in FNA, palmately (5–)7(–9)-lobed nearly to the base; lobes lance-elliptic with irregularly sinuate, crenate, dentate, or pinnatifid margins.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Flowers usually solitary, sometimes in small 2–3-flowered cymes.
morphology_keys.sepals: Oblong, about 18–25 mm, mucronate, enlarging/persisting around the fruit.
morphology_keys.corolla: White with a purplish/rose-purple throat, usually about 30–45 mm long.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule about 1–2 cm, surrounded by an enlarged persistent calyx; seeds black and glabrous.
morphology_keys.flowering: April–November in Flora of North America.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: The deeply palmately dissected leaf is immediately striking; confirm with the white flower with purple throat and long persistent sepals.
fastest_traits: White funnel-shaped flower with purple throat

look_alikes.distinction: Several Ipomoea have lobed leaves, but D. dissectus combines extremely dissected leaves, long sepals, white/purple-throated flowers, and spirally twisted anthers.

ecology.habitat: Disturbed/open sites and roadsides; tolerates poor and alkaline soils when well drained.
ecology.texas_note: Austin's native plant guide lists Alamo vine for local use; historical Texas floras treated it as native at least as far north as Travis County.

photo_strategy.method: One API request fetches research-grade observations with photos, then the downloader saves the first photo from five different observations at large resolution.
